description: Where each Jetpack Settings hash route and ?term= search goes once the Settings screen retires. Nothing reads it yet: the redirect document that page=jetpack-settings and the page=jetpack forwarder (Jetpack_React_Page) will print resolves these rules in PHP, since the server never sees the hash. It applies only while Initializer::is_settings_consolidation_enabled() is true. The Network Admin jetpack-settings page is out of scope. It is production-excluded in .gitattributes; the PR that first reads it must remove that exclusion.
matching: `everySource` runs before any route or term rule. A term matches its decoded value, case-insensitively, before its route; an unmatched term falls back to its route. On page=jetpack-settings, an empty hash (the bare menu link) or an unknown route gets the /settings rules, as main.jsx does. On page=jetpack, an unknown route never reaches these rules: the forwarder (Jetpack_React_Page::get_legacy_route_redirects()) sends it to My Jetpack for admins and to Settings for everyone else, as it does today, so #/my-plan, #/dashboard and #/stats keep landing on My Jetpack. In each list, the first rule whose `when` all hold wins, and a rule without `when` is the default. A rule with `pending` keeps the source on Settings until each marker clears: `D<n>` is an open decision, `JETPACK-<n>` an issue that must land, `flag:<name>` a feature flag that must retire, `error-notice-home` a page that shows the Jetpack::state( 'error' ) notice where My Jetpack doesn't (to users who can't open it, offline, and during onboarding), and `monetize-page` a Monetize page that shows the Ads settings (its flag on and the `monetize` module active), without which the Ads settings stay on Settings. A `destination` next to `pending` is where the source goes once it clears. A settings panel destination (`configure=`) waits on the issue that gives the panel that module's settings, since until then the panel's fallback links back here through configure_url. Destinations are relative to wp-admin. My Jetpack `#/` links work on every My Jetpack version, since its router rewrites them to `?p=`.

decisions.D7: Where Google Analytics settings go on Atomic sites where the settings panel does not offer them (googleAnalyticsPanel is false).
decisions.D9: Where users who cannot manage modules find Publicize and their own account connection, since Features needs manage_options. Post by Email stays on their Profile page.
decisions.D10: What happens to the legacy SEO block on self-hosted sites that have not opted in to the SEO page.
decisions.D11: Where the per-user usage tracking (Privacy) setting lives.

conditions.partnerCoupon: Jetpack_React_Page::get_partner_coupon_redirect() returns a URL; that screen takes every route.
conditions.error: Jetpack::state( 'error' ) is set. Elsewhere than My Jetpack (see settingsNoticesInMyJetpack), Settings is the only screen that shows it.
conditions.settingsNoticesInMyJetpack: The user can open My Jetpack (Jetpack_React_Page::can_use_my_jetpack()) and Automattic\Jetpack\My_Jetpack\Initializer::shows_settings_notices() is true: settings consolidation is on, and My Jetpack is neither offline nor sending the user to onboarding.
conditions.canManageModules: The user has jetpack_manage_modules. Users without it reach Settings only for Publicize, since Post by Email stays on their Profile page.
conditions.protectPage: did_action( 'jetpack_protect_dashboard_initialized' ) (siteData.hasProtectPage): the protect-dashboard module or the connected Jetpack Protect plugin registered the Protect page. Not Automattic\Jetpack\My_Jetpack\Products\Protect::has_protect_page(), which is also true while the plugin shows its own page.
conditions.socialPage: Publicize registered admin.php?page=jetpack-social for this user (siteData.hasSocialPage), which its host, connection and jetpack_publicize_should_load filter decide.
conditions.adsSettingsHome: Jetpack_Ads_Settings_Home::is_moved_off_settings(): settings consolidation is on and the Monetize page shows the Ads settings.
conditions.analyticsDashboard: Automattic\Jetpack\PremiumAnalytics\Analytics::is_initialized(): Stats v2 booted, from Jetpack (Jetpack::is_premium_analytics_enabled()) or the Premium Analytics plugin, and is the site's analytics UI (script data analytics.enabled).
conditions.settingsTabsLeft: Jetpack_Settings_React_Page::get_remaining_tabs() lists a tab (siteData.settingsTabs), so Settings keeps its sidebar entry. Without one, the entry is hidden.

moduleTerms: Every module slug below is also linked by Jetpack::module_configuration_url(), the Configure link in Features and the classic Modules list, unless the module filters that URL.
protectTerms: The waf, protect, account-protection, sso and monitor destinations copy Automattic\Jetpack\Protect\Dashboard::get_module_settings_urls(); call it rather than hard-coding them. Without the Protect page, they and /security open the Protect card on Features, which turns the page on.
